scope: Current Linux/WSL public HTTP2 fixed-body connection episodes; not a current cross-platform ranking or an inference-engine test.

method.cpu: All formal consumers and both persistent workers inherit Linux logical CPU2 affinity.
method.configured_resources: One Hyle Scheduler worker plus one direct nghttp2 worker; both harnesses exist in every process, one route active at a time. Actual userspace thread snapshots were not collected.
method.timed: Fresh nonblocking Unix socket pair, 4KiB socket buffers, both HTTP2 sessions, full header/body work and exact checks, reverse pair response completion, body acknowledgements at both flow-control levels, session/socket destruction and external completion handoff.
method.not_charged: Persistent harness construction/destruction, fixed workload-body string generation, one untimed preflight per route, optional JSON serialization after each workload.
method.normal: 64 streams, two active at a time, 1KiB request and response each, 1MiB connection receive window.
method.holdout: 4 streams, two active at a time, 256KiB request and response each, 65535-byte connection window.
method.sampling: Four processes per formal phase, two execution orders. Nine nanobench epochs per route/workload, at least five complete episodes per epoch. No samples filtered; no cross-process CI or equivalence conclusion.

fairness_fix: Peer raw_advance formerly rescanned every completed pair on every protocol turn. A monotonic next_response_pair now skips pairs after both reverse-ordered responses have been submitted; all DATA/write/consume/validation/teardown work remains.
current_result: With corrected peer wrapper, 64x1KiB is faster for Hyle in all four initial processes; 4x256KiB is slower by 5.59-8.27%. Do not inherit historical WIN/PARITY or the old 5% practical pass rule.
aa_limit: One scratch-only process per same route, both labels run the same Hyle or peer call. Second-position holdout advantage approximately 5.04% Hyle / 2.66% peer. These are observed position/warm-state differences, not correction factors, CIs, hardware timer resolution, or proof that the formal residual is noise.

candidate.description: Do not notify again when releasing the immediate read-direction claim; process_received already published input changes. Async read path unchanged.
candidate.tests: 13 current HTTP2/feature tests pass, plus separate forced-epoll duplex test. Both rebuilt baseline and candidate smoke return 64/64/4/4.
candidate.comparison: Both protocol TUs rebuilt against the same then-current headers because unrelated container headers changed during this task. Foundation shared cache and peer/consumer objects identical. Two baseline/candidate order pairs retained without filtering.
candidate.result: Not an established speedup: one holdout candidate point is slower, the other close in absolute Hyle time, while peer times drift. Reverted product source to original; frozen candidate and raw logs retained. Holdout residual remains unresolved.

identity_limits: Only nghttp2_static and current HTTP/HTTP2/consumer TUs built. Foundation libraries reused from io-watch-v2-dev and hashed; this is not a full HEAD rebuild. Initial formal and later candidate phase header environments differ and must not be directly attributed to the notify change.

nghttp2.build: Existing locked source, lib-only/static/Release/GCC14, no downloads, no SDK staging or Hyle CMake configure.
